title: Flash Gordon

evidence.note: UNVERIFIED. The archive.org item page for the Catalog of Copyright Entries, Third Series, Parts 12-13, Motion Pictures and Filmstrips, Jan-Dec 1964 (Volume 18, Nos. 1-2) was fetched. Only the item's metadata and download links were read. No page or section of the volume text was read, and no 'FLASH GORDON' entry was seen. An earlier draft reported an index line 'FLASH GORDON. (R)' and named a filer, and it also quoted a chapter title, dates and an R-number. None of these could be re-read, so they are withdrawn. The filer is unconfirmed. The renewal entry, its page, its text and its registration details are all unconfirmed. This record does not establish that the serial was renewed, or that it was not. Next step: open the 1964 volume's full text, find the 'FLASH GORDON' renewal entry, and record the page and exact entry text.

evidence.note: Wikipedia says the serial's music was recycled from several other films: Bride of Frankenstein (1935), Bombay Mail (1934), The Black Cat (1934), Werewolf of London (1935) and The Invisible Man (1933). This Wikipedia citation supports the music-reuse claim only. It shows nothing about the copyright status of the score. That status is not established. It depends on the status of those source scores and on the serial's own status. None of these has been checked.

Based on Alex Raymond's Flash Gordon comic strip, first published in 1934, and made with King Features Syndicate. The strip's 1934 start means its copyright has not expired by term. The strip's own renewal and status were not checked.

editorial:
Flash Gordon is a 13-chapter science-fiction serial from Universal, released April 6, 1936 and directed by Frederick Stephani. It stars Buster Crabbe. It is based on the character created by Alex Raymond in 1934.

The rights question here is renewal, and it is not settled. The 1964 Catalog of Copyright Entries was checked only at the item-page level. No renewal entry for the serial was read, so the film's renewal is unconfirmed. The comic strip's renewal has not been checked either. The music was recycled from earlier films whose status has not been checked. Copies on the Internet Archive are not evidence of public-domain status. Verify the film, the score and the strip before any reuse.
faq: Is the 1936 Flash Gordon serial public domain?
Unknown. The 1964 Catalog of Copyright Entries was not read at the entry level, so the film's renewal is unconfirmed. Copies on the Internet Archive do not show public-domain status.
Can I use Flash Gordon characters or the name in a new work?

Not without checking. The serial is based on Alex Raymond's character, created in 1934. Universal produced and distributed the serial. The strip's renewal status, any King Features rights and any trademarks have not been checked, and they may be separate from the film.
